properties.requirement: Identify the authorization checks and branches for the authenticated user, the requested document, and the selected version or original/archive representation

Determine whether selecting another document version or choosing original versus archive changes the resource on which authorization is evaluated, or only changes the representation or file returned after authorization

questions.reason: The question asks for evidence limits and missing facts rather than asserting a narrow authorization or completion property.

statements.because: The explicit download authorization check evaluates the requesting user.
The requested row is normalized to its root document and that root is passed to the permission check.
The effective selected document supplies the returned source or archive file.
A failed owner-aware view check returns Forbidden; only its successful branch continues.
serve_file constructs the download from the selected effective document, choosing archive when requested by the branch.
The effective file document is the requested version row when the path pk identifies a version and no version query parameter exists; otherwise it is resolved within the root family.
A file response is reached only after request/root resolution and the successful root-document owner-aware check.

diagnostics.message: Basic finite predicates: {op:"eq"|"neq",left:<operand>,right:<operand>}, {op:"is-null",value:<operand>}, {op:"all"|"any",args:[<predicate>,...]}, {op:"not",arg:<predicate>}. Use all/any rather than and/or. An operand is {literal:<finite value>}, {binding:<source name or field>}, or {lookup:{map:<operand>,key:<operand>}}. These exact fields are required; free-text or unsupported operators are rejected, never coerced into a condition. Additional finite predicates: {op:"member",value:<operand>,set:<operand>}, {op:"has-key",map:<operand>,key:<operand>}, {op:"gt"|"gte"|"lt"|"lte",left:<operand>,right:<operand>,order?:[source-supported ordered scalars]}. Operands are {literal:scalar|scalar[]|map<string,scalar>}, {binding:name}, or {lookup:{map:<operand>,key:<operand>}}. Finite sets/maps have at most64 entries. Numeric comparisons need no order; other ordering requires an explicit source-supported order, never inferred role names. Missing map keys are errors rather than null; has-key explicitly tests absence. Unknown user values remain residual. Short-circuit skips later evaluation errors, but invalid syntax is rejected. Parameterized object fields use binding:"object.field"; host substitutes actual invocation identities from explicit arguments. Values on one object never apply to another. For operation shared source, values may name questionId and are still exact current user premises.
